# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual specifies the defusal rule for the wire: the wire cut depends on the light color at the moment of the cut (purple -> green, red -> blue, white -> yellow). 

As Mute, I cannot speak and cannot touch the bomb; I can only communicate via gestures to Deaf, who can see but cannot hear. Blind can touch the bomb and hear speech, but cannot see gestures. Deaf can see the bomb and speak to Blind and me. 

Since "a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something," and Deaf cannot hear any explanation from me, Deaf must first observe the bomb and establish a protocol or ask a structured question via speech. Once Deaf describes the bomb's layout and suggests a signalling convention, I will signal the appropriate response.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Ready. Deaf speaks the bomb state, you gesture the wire number to Deaf, Deaf speaks it aloud, and I cut.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display is 0. Light is white. Wires: 1 is yellow, 2 is green, 3 is blue. Blind: feel the bomb and speak aloud anything you find so Mute can hear. Mute: signal me with ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or other clear gestures.

The manual states that the wire to cut depends strictly on the light's color at the moment of the cut, and that the light changes every round, walking a circle of three colours (purple -> green, red -> blue, white -> yellow).

In Round 1, Deaf observed the light was white, and the wires were 1: yellow, 2: green, 3: blue. Deaf established a signalling convention for the wires: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3.

Because the turn order in each round is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf:
- Deaf's speech reaches Blind and me at the start of the next round.
- If I were to signal a wire to Deaf now in Round 2, Deaf would only speak it at the end of Round 2, meaning Blind would cut in Round 3.
- In Round 3, the light will not be white (as it cycles through three colors every round: Round 1 is white, Round 2 and Round 3 are the other two colors, and Round 4 will return to white). Cutting wire 1 (yellow) in Round 3 would detonate the bomb.
- Furthermore, I do not yet know the direction of the color cycle (whether Round 2 is purple or red), so I cannot predict Round 3's light color either without guessing.

Therefore, I must wait this round. Deaf will observe the light change in Round 2 and report the new state. In Round 3, I can signal wire 1 (☝) to Deaf, Deaf will instruct Blind at the end of Round 3, and Blind will cut wire 1 in Round 4 when the light cycles back to white.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No tactile marks or textures felt on the bomb. Waiting for Deaf to read your gesture.
Deaf says: Update: The light just changed to PURPLE! Display is still 0. Wires are still: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, please gesture to me when you have an instruction: ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, or gesture if you need something else.

Deaf observed the light was White in round 1 and Purple in round 2. Given that the light cycles through three colours (White, Purple, Red), it will be Red in round 3 and White again in round 4. 

When I gesture to Deaf in round 3, Deaf will receive it at the end of round 3 and instruct Blind. Blind will then execute the cut during round 4, when the light is White. According to the manual, a White light requires cutting the yellow wire (wire 1).

Following Deaf's mapping (☝ for wire 1):

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| purple | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute gestured ☝! Cut wire 1 (the first wire / yellow wire)! Also, light is now RED, display is 0.

I have already gestured ☝ to Deaf in Turn 3, and Deaf has instructed Blind to cut wire 1 (yellow wire). Blind will execute the cut in Round 4, which is when the light cycles back to White. No further signals are needed.

```
wait()
```
